mentions.name: 1980s Japanese arcade cabinet resto-mod
mentions.description: This project resto-mods a 1980s Japanese arcade cabinet to make it compatible with most any game that would have run on such a cab. The original 15kHz CRT was revived by recapping its board, and the rebuilt control panel uses RGB-lit buttons that change color per loaded game, controlled by an ESP-32s2 that emulates a keyboard and accepts serial messages from the host. A Stream Deck integrated in the control panel runs a custom Node application for auxiliary functions on Linux, where no OEM software exists. The main challenge is getting a suitable signal to the CRT: attempts included Raspberry Pi GPIO through a VGA666 board (limited to 16-bit color) and a downscaler (24-bit color but no resolution switching), with an AMD system currently being tested since its Linux driver can set custom 15kHz/25kHz resolutions from the VGA port. A writeup is planned near completion.
mentions.problem: The original control panel was unsalvageable and insufficient for running a wide range of games, and getting a suitable video signal to the 15kHz CRT was difficult — GPIO output capped colors at 16-bit, and downscaling prevented resolution switching.
